ledger.failureMode: Phase 2 step 4 of the author-playwright-tests command says to carry the framework forward as the string nunit when detectE2eFrameworkInDir returns null (no recognised test package in the .csproj files under the project directory, both frameworks, or references that come only from an imported props file), and Phase 4 step 3 hands that value to writeOrAppendSpecFile as specDetails.framework. In spec-writer, appendTestMethod treats any framework that was passed in as an explicit request and throws a framework mismatch error when inferFramework on the existing file says xunit, so the defaulted nunit makes landing a test into an existing xUnit spec file fail after the QA engineer has already accepted and run it. The inference from the file, which exists for a caller that passes no framework, is never reached through this command, and the proposal request is told nunit even though the validateProposalRequest contract says to omit framework when it is unknown.
ledger.evidence: Read packages/e2e-testing/commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml:151 (Execution Setup, step Ensure the Screenshot Helper: 'carry the result forward as framework ("nunit" when it returns null)') and the Land step (generated copy commands/ensemble/author-playwright-tests.md:184: 'writeOrAppendSpecFile(filePath, specDetails) ... with specDetails.framework'; the Phase 3 proposal request action likewise sends framework). lib/spec-writer.js:418-424: requested = specDetails.framework === undefined ? undefined : resolveFramework(specDetails); inferred = inferFramework(existingContent); it throws when requested && inferred && requested !== inferred. lib/delegation-contract.js:50-52 documents framework as 'Omit when unknown (NUnit)'. tests/spec-writer-xunit.test.js:198-201 shows a caller that gives no framework gets xunit inferred from the file, and :211-212 shows an explicit 'nunit' on an xUnit file is refused, so the two cases are meant to differ and the command collapses unknown into explicit. lib/e2e-framework.js:12 and :33-48 only read PackageReference elements of .csproj files under the directory, so null is reachable for projects whose test packages come from an imported Directory.Build.props, and for projects referencing both frameworks. packages/e2e-testing/CHANGELOG.md:21 promises that appending to an existing file infers its framework and that NUnit stays the default when the framework cannot be told; through this command the explicit default wins over the inference. I ran a throwaway snippet (node -e, requiring the snapshot's lib/spec-writer.js) on a minimal xUnit class file with using Xunit and one [Fact] method: writeOrAppendSpec(file, framework nunit, testName N, acId AC-1) printed "framework mismatch: the existing file uses xunit but framework 'nunit' was requested."; the same call with framework omitted appended a method and printed "omitted framework: appended as xunit". Suggested fix: in Phase 2 step 4 (yaml:151) and the Phase 3 request action, leave framework unset when detection returns null, so a new file still defaults to NUnit and an append infers from the existing file.

A body that relies on a namespace the siblings import (for example FluentAssertions for .Should(), or a shared helper namespace) or on a differently named fixture field is therefore written into a new file that lacks that using or field, and no step of the landing phase compiles the new file.

ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework treats a package as a framework marker when its lower-cased id merely starts with nunit or xunit, so framework-agnostic test loggers such as NunitXml.TestLogger or XunitXml.TestLogger set the other framework flag; an xUnit project that also references NunitXml.TestLogger has both flags set, the function returns null, and the command then carries null forward as nunit, so the xUnit project gets NUnit attributes and a PageTest-style body.
ledger.evidence: Ran a throwaway snippet against the snapshot's lib/e2e-framework.js: detectE2eFramework over PackageReference ids xunit, Microsoft.Playwright, NunitXml.TestLogger printed null; over NUnit, Microsoft.Playwright.NUnit, XunitXml.TestLogger it also printed null (that case lands on the NUnit fallback by luck). The command (commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml:151) carries 'nunit' forward when the result is null, with no prompt to the QA engineer. Matching the id followed by a dot, a digit or its end (nunit, nunit3testadapter, nunit.analyzers; xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, xunit.v3) or an explicit list of the framework packages would exclude both loggers. Same run: a single-quoted attribute (Include='xunit') is not read either (null). tests/e2e-framework.test.js covers neither input. The trigger is an uncommon package, so the severity is a judgment call.

ledger.failureMode: The loop that checks every $E2E_LIB/<module>.js the command names exists in lib/ builds its module list with the pattern /\$E2E_LIB\/([a-z-]+)\.js/g. The character class has no digits, so a name such as e2e-framework (the new module, named in author-playwright-tests.yaml line 151) never matches and is never looked at by that loop: deleting lib/e2e-framework.js would leave this test green. Only the separate existsSync in author-playwright-tests-framework.test.js covers this one file, and any later module with a digit in its name is skipped the same way.
ledger.evidence: Read the pattern at author-playwright-tests-evidence.test.js:68 and the separate check at author-playwright-tests-framework.test.js:60. Ran the same matchAll over the snapshot's commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml in a throwaway node script: with [a-z-]+ it found 22 module names and seen.has('e2e-framework') printed false; with [a-z0-9-]+ it found 23, the extra one being e2e-framework. The line was not edited by this change, but the new digit-named module is what makes it blind.

ledger.failureMode: The inferFramework case labelled 'only in a string' feeds the source var s = "using Xunit;"; and expects null, but it passes whether or not string literals are masked: the using pattern in inferFramework is anchored to a line start (^[ \t]*(?:global\s+)?using\s+Xunit\s*;) and this line starts with var, so the pattern cannot match the unmasked text either, and the attribute pattern finds no [Fact] or [Theory] in it. If inferFramework stopped masking string literals this case would still pass, so the doc comment's statement that string literals are ignored has no test that can fail; a string literal that holds [Fact] would discriminate.
ledger.evidence: Read inferFramework (spec-writer.js:106-113) and the case at spec-writer-xunit.test.js:250. Ran the two patterns inferFramework uses directly on that source string without masking: both printed false, and inferFramework(source) printed null, so the case cannot tell masked from unmasked. The neighbouring 'only in a comment' case does discriminate, because its block comment carries [Fact].

ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework counts the Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit package as xunit (pinned by the test at e2e-framework.test.js line 30), but the xunit mode serves only one project shape. spec-writer.js scaffoldXunitFile always emits a [Collection] class with a constructor-injected fixture and throws unless the caller supplies collection and fixtureType, and agents/playwright-tester.yaml line 61 tells the author that framework xunit means no PageTest Page. Playwright's own xUnit base class is a PageTest that exposes Page, and a project built on it has no collection name or fixture class to copy, so for that project the authoring guidance contradicts its sibling tests and a new spec file cannot be written (the scaffold throws). The CHANGELOG scopes support to core Microsoft.Playwright with a [Collection] fixture, but neither the detector nor the agent sentence says so.
ledger.evidence: Read e2e-framework.js:25, spec-writer.js:217-251 (scaffoldXunitFile) and agents/playwright-tester.yaml:61. Ran detectE2eFramework on a project file whose only reference is Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit: it printed 'xunit'. Ran scaffoldNewSpecFile with framework 'xunit', className, testName and a Page-based testBody but no collection: it threw "collection must be the project's xUnit collection name (got: undefined) -- copy it from a sibling spec class." The Playwright .NET docs (https://playwright.dev/dotnet/docs/test-runners) list provided base classes for xUnit and xUnit v3, which is what a PageTest-based xUnit project uses. Appending to an existing file of such a project still works, so only the new-file path and the guidance sentence are affected.

ledger.failureMode: The xUnit wording added to the Land step, and to the authoring agent text, leaves out part of the contract between the authored test and the generated class. The step says a new xunit file needs {collection, fixtureType} copied from a sibling spec class, but writeOrAppendSpecFile also refuses every xunit method, new or appended, that has no specDetails.testBody, and neither the step nor the agent text says that the confirmed proposedTest is what goes into testBody. For a new class, scaffoldXunitFile always declares the injected fixture as a private field named _fixture with a constructor parameter named fixture, while the agent is only told to build the context and page as the project's sibling tests do: if the sibling names its fixture field differently, a body written against that name is landed inside a class that has no such member. The Land step's own actions (writeOrAppendSpecFile, tagTestMethod, logAction) never build the file, so the error would first surface when the PR is built.

ledger.failureMode: When detectE2eFramework cannot decide (it returns null if the PackageReference names match both frameworks or neither, and it matches by name prefix, so any package whose name merely starts with nunit or xunit counts), the command turns that null into an explicit framework 'nunit' and passes it on, both in the Proposal request and as specDetails.framework when landing. appendTestMethod treats an explicit framework as authoritative and throws 'framework mismatch' for an existing xUnit spec file, although inferFramework on that file would have given the right answer had framework been omitted; the Proposal request also carries 'nunit', so the authoring agent gets no instruction to build its own page. Omitting framework when detection returns null would let the existing file decide.
ledger.evidence: Read e2e-framework.js lines 23-28 (prefix match on the lower-cased package name; 'if (nunit === xunit) return null'), the command action at author-playwright-tests.yaml:151 ('carry the result forward as framework ("nunit" when it returns null)') and the landing action at :226 ('with specDetails.framework'), spec-writer.js:418-424 (requested = specDetails.framework, inferred = inferFramework(existingContent), throw when both are set and differ, otherwise requested || inferred || 'nunit'), and delegation-contract.js:50-52 (the framework field says 'Omit when unknown (NUnit)', so omission is the contract's own way to say unknown). The e2e-framework header and both CHANGELOG entries state that NUnit is the fallback, so this is a design call rather than a coding slip, and it only bites when detection is ambiguous.
